_doc: Conversations. Talking to someone opens a menu of questions. Each question is asked once per loop. learn: adds that clue to the board. tip: points the Lead at that clue (and says where to find it). when: only offered while this holds. Social moves from interactions.json with talk:true appear in the same menu (gold), or greyed with their 'notYet' text when the moment isn't right.

ashcombe.line: A toast, on stage, at five to twelve! And a little announcement. You'll want to be there.

ashcombe.ask: Who's the man in the white jacket?
ashcombe.line: Calloway. My banker. And, er... my very good friend, these days.
Me? Nonsense. I've a little business with Calloway by the study fire at a quarter to nine, that's all.

vivienne.line: Dolly Vane. Edmund booked her. She sings at ten. I'd give my pearls for her not to.
Edmund's been odd all week. Keeps slipping into the study with that banker.
Inspector Hale sees everything. Mrs Pryce prints everything. And Brock simply hits things. Behave where they can see you.

calloway.line: Silas Calloway. I own the bank. After tonight, rather more than the bank.
Later. Half past seven, at the champagne tower. Champagne makes me sentimental. And numerical.
Is it? I wouldn't know. I certainly shan't be out there at seven o'clock.

dolly.line: Ten o'clock, sugar. One song, one microphone, no encores.
Every night. I practise on the balcony when the party starts, in case a picture man is listening.
One microphone, one cable. If that cable goes, I go home early.
Starving. I'll sneak some cake from the kitchen at half nine. Don't tell the chef.

rupert.line: Pictures, old boy. I'm practically in pictures. Well. I've seen several.
Oh, this and that. Mostly that. Ask me again when you've met someone worth impressing.
Uncle's making an announcement at midnight. Ghastly. He's been playing cards with that banker again.
That Inspector's been scribbling about me all evening. Get me that notebook, would you? There's a fiver in it. Well. An IOU for a fiver.

hale.line: Allegedly. Do something shady where I can see it and I'll whistle for Brock. Where I can't see it... well. I'm off duty.
The butler naps in the kitchen at eight. Keys and naps don't mix.
Notes. Habit. I like a quiet chair by the library fire after dinner, and I like it to stay quiet.
Have we... no. Carry on. Odd evening. Feels like I've had this conversation before.

pryce.line: Darling, the banker has a secret. I'd know. I'm in it. ...Forget I said that.
Books, a fire, and a safe behind the sunset painting. Not that I've looked. Much.

hobbs.line: Private, sir. I unlock it for His Lordship at a quarter to nine and lock it again at half past nine.
I rest my eyes in the kitchen at eight, sir. The study key never leaves my pocket.
It hangs on one rope behind the right-hand stage curtain, sir. I check the knot annually.

pierre.line: Always, monsieur. Nobody looks at a waiter. There is a spare jacket by the kitchen door, if monsieur wishes to vanish.

pierre.ask: Can I take a glass to His Lordship?
pierre.line: A guest? Non. His Lordship only takes a glass from staff. Twenty to twelve, at the tower.

marcel.line: The soufflé. With my tonic! Three drops and the critics sleep like babies. It is by the stove. Do NOT touch.

marcel.ask: Do you ever take a break?
marcel.line: Half past ten, one cigarette, in the corner. The rest of the night: OUT of my kitchen.

brock.line: Somebody shouts, I come running. I catch you, you're out. Can't catch what's quicker than me, mind.
I walk the ballroom every half hour. No trouble tonight.
Fire bell's by the library door. Anyone rings it, everybody lines up in this hall and I count heads. Twice.

elsie.line: So many stairs. At least there's the little door from the kitchen into the study. Saves my knees.

elsie.ask: Do the lights ever go out?
elsie.line: Only if someone pulls the main fuse. It's in the kitchen, on the wall by the window. Ten minutes of pitch dark.
